# Integration Design Document (IDD) - the .xlsm template for integrations

For traditional Workday integrations (EIB, Studio, Core Connector, DT, O4I-delivered-as-INT), the design doc is the IDD, not the Extend templates.

## Getting an IDD - regenerate the structure from text, or obtain the branded macro master

This skill no longer ships a proprietary binary master. Two paths, and the split matters because **the IDD's macro/formula/shape behavior cannot be reliably regenerated by a script:**

1. **Regenerate a working STRUCTURAL template from text** (default, always available, cross-platform) - `python scripts/build_idd_structure.py [out.xlsx]`. It lays down all **22 sheets** in order with the correct visibility (O4I default), each tab title, section-band headings, primary column-header rows, the Overview Key Details block, the Unit Testing status summary, and the **READ ME as cells** (reusing the canonical content from `scripts/write_idd_readme.py`). Output is neutral/unbranded - style it with `scripts/xlsx_brand_style.py`.
   - **HARD LIMIT - this is a structural `.xlsx`, NOT the macro `.xlsm`.** Three things are ABSENT because they cannot come from text (openpyxl row-writes and COM rebuilds both drop shapes/macros - **exactly what dropped the READ ME + macro on delivered IDDs**): **(a)** the VBA Integration-Type visibility macro (Overview!J10) - all solution sheets are simply present, set visibility by hand; **(b)** the ISU/ISSG auto-naming formulas and other Overview!J8/J9 CONCAT formulas - those are blank cells to type; **(c)** the READ ME **text box** (we write the durable **cell** form instead). Use this skeleton for a working structural doc; do not pretend it fires macros.

2. **Obtain the branded macro master per engagement** (when you need the true `.xlsm` with macro + formulas + shapes intact) - pull it from the engagement store (see the environment memory), verify the READ ME and the Integration-Type macro fire, keep it in the engagement's store, and fill it per the order below. Do **not** re-bundle it into this skill.

(The legacy `.xlsm` masters that once lived under `assets/` have been relocated OUT of this skill - `assets/` now holds only the READ-ME content file. If you find an `.xlsm` in a stale copy of this skill, treat it as non-canonical.) See [template-builder.md](template-builder.md) for both paths and for the customer-rebrand mechanisms (`scripts/xlsx_brand_style.py --brand-profile <client>`, and `scripts/rebrand_template.py`, which preserves an existing macro workbook's VBA/formulas).

## The IDD is a design doc - it inherits the FULL Extend rulebook

An IDD is not exempt from the conventions in SKILL.md just because it's an integration and macro-driven. Apply every one, with integration-appropriate adjustments. These were being missed on delivered IDDs (2026-08-04) - treat them as gate items:

- **Yellow-highlight open / unanswered cells, with a note, on EVERY tab** - not just the Question tab. Any cell awaiting a decision, a vendor answer, a WID, an endpoint, a payload detail gets the solid FFFF00 fill + text stating the question/owner (per SKILL.md's yellow convention). Remove the fill when answered. A blank cell that should hold something is a miss; a yellow cell tells the reader exactly what's still needed.
- **"N/A" for reviewed-and-not-applicable - never leave it blank.** If a field, row, or whole tab genuinely doesn't apply to this integration, write **`N/A`** (optionally "N/A - <one-word reason>"). Blank = "nobody looked"; N/A = "reviewed, intentionally not applicable." This is how the reader tells the difference. Applies to Key Details fields, per-tab sections, and unused solution sheets.
- **Sweep cell-by-cell WITHIN every populated row - not just row-by-row.** A row that has ANY content is a "populated row," and EVERY cell in it (across the table's real column span) must be non-blank: a value, `N/A`, or yellow-TBD. This is the miss that keeps recurring - e.g., on the API tab a documented element row had its Hard Coded Value / Sample Value / Format cells left blank while only the row's Notes cell was flagged. Per-column rule of thumb: a column that legitimately doesn't apply to that row -> **N/A** (e.g., Hard Coded Value on a read/write op); a column that SHOULD hold info you don't have yet -> **yellow "TBD - <what's needed>"** (e.g., a missing Sample Value or Format you'd normally capture). Do NOT flag cells outside the table's real column span (unlabeled columns past the last header) or empty unused scaffolding rows (a row with only its sequence number) - trim/ignore those, don't N/A every empty cell.
  - **Enforce this MECHANICALLY - do not eyeball it.** Fresh sessions keep missing interior blanks, so this is now a hard gate: run **`python scripts/idd_audit.py <idd.xlsm>`** before delivery. It flags the "odd-one-out" (a row that's a full member of a table but is missing a column its peers fill - exactly this bug), confirms the READ ME sheet has content, and reports every yellow open cell. Resolve each hit (value / `N/A` / yellow-with-a-note) until it reports `[ok] no interior blanks` and `[ok] READ ME has cell content`. It skips form/prose tabs (Overview, Question, Instructions, Flow, Examples) and dashboard blocks by design; use `--skip "Tab A,Tab B"` for any additional structural tab.
- **Clean up unused template rows and sample/placeholder data.** The template ships pre-numbered rows and worked examples; a delivered IDD must not carry empty scaffolding or someone else's sample. Specifically: on the **API tab, clear the Status column for rows with no documented element** (e.g., rows 24-50 if only 1-23 are used - don't leave "Researching" on empty rows); delete the **Calculated Fields** example rows, the **Custom Object** bookstore example, and any File/Report/DIS sample rows once real content is in. Either populate a row or remove it - no orphaned "Researching"/half-filled rows.
- **READ ME is authored as CELLS, not a text box (this is the durable fix).** The READ ME content (the macro-enable steps + Step 1-4 + TIPS) is the integration counterpart of the Extend template's Instructions tab and MUST be present on every IDD. **Root cause of the repeated "READ ME is missing" defects:** the template historically carried it as a floating **text-box shape**, and shapes are dropped by every build path except a clean Excel-COM copy (openpyxl rewrites, partial rebuilds) - so a new IDD kept losing it. **Fix (2026-08-04):** the READ ME is now written as **formatted worksheet cells**, which survive EVERY path (COM *and* openpyxl preserve cell values + styles). A current firm-store master already carries the cell-based READ ME; the canonical text lives in `assets/idd-readme-content.md`.
  - **To (re)apply it to any IDD:** `python scripts/write_idd_readme.py <idd.xlsm>` - it deletes any legacy READ ME shape and writes the content as cells (dark-blue bold title, blue instructions, a dark banner for the macro steps), with fit-to-1-page-wide page setup so nothing clips. Uses Excel COM (preserves VBA/other sheets); Windows + Excel.
  - **Do NOT reintroduce the text box.** If you copy the master you inherit the cells; if you produce an IDD any other way, run the script.
  - **Save the view at the top-left (A1).** A workbook remembers its scroll position; if the READ ME sheet was saved scrolled right (e.g. near column AA), it OPENS on empty cells and looks blank even though the text is in B:L. `write_idd_readme.py` now resets the view to A1 before saving - if you touch the sheet by hand, scroll back to A1 and put the cursor on A1 before saving.
  - **Verify by RENDER, never a shape/text check** - export the sheet to PDF/PNG (or run the audit below, which mechanically confirms the READ ME sheet has cell content).
- **Flow tab is mandatory and has TWO diagrams** (see the expanded Flow row below): the **This-Integration process flow** at minimum, plus a **Broader Landscape** when the integration is part of a package.
- **Examples tab holds real OBJECT ATTACHMENTS** - embed sample scripts, vendor docs, sample files (PII-scrubbed), XSLT, SOAP req/resp as embedded objects in the sheet, not just references (see the expanded Examples row).
- **General formatting** (SKILL.md): bordered tables, no light-gray grids, gridlines off outside content, embedded diagrams in their own clear block not overlapping cells, one blank row between sections, fresh-eyes pass per tab.

## How the template works (macro-driven - fill order matters)

1. **Overview tab FIRST.** The Key Details block (col I labels / col J values) drives everything: **Integration Type (J10) fires a `Worksheet_Change` macro that hides/unhides the matching solution sheets** (O4I -> `WD Solution - O4I`; Studio/EIB -> `WD Solution - General`; Connector/Connector+DT -> `WD Solution - CC` + `Field Overrides - CC` + `Mappings - CC`). Integration ID (J8) + Name (J9) auto-build the ISU/ISSG names by formula (`ISU <ID> <Name>` / `ISSG <ID> <Name>`) - so get J8/J9 right before touching security sections. Open the file in Excel (macros enabled) for the type switch; openpyxl edits with `keep_vba=True` but won't fire the macro - set the type in Excel first.
   - **Filling via Excel COM? Disable events during the fill, then set tab visibility explicitly afterward.** Writing Integration Type (J10) mid-fill fires the `Worksheet_Change` visibility macro, which re-shows the Connector / General / CC solution tabs you don't want (e.g. for an O4I). Set `Application.EnableEvents = False` while writing, then after the fill set each solution tab's `.Visible` yourself (~9 tabs hidden for an O4I IDD). And once the INT ID (J8) is set the template **AUTO-NAMES the ISU/ISSG by formula** (`ISSG <INT ID> ...` / `ISU <INT ID> ...`) - leave those formula cells alone; don't overwrite them with literals.
2. **Question tab** - ~50 pre-seeded vendor/discovery questions (General, Overview, File Retrieval, Data/File, Integration Specific, Testing, Go Live), each with Status (Have to ask / Open question / Answered), Answer, and why-it-matters. This is the integration counterpart of the Discovery tab; the yellow-highlight convention applies to unanswered rows, and the design gate is "all statuses Answered, highlights removed."
3. **Version Control** - start with an "Initial Draft" row; log every functional change (Version, Date, Editor, High Level + Detail summaries).
4. Then the rest, per integration type.

## Sheet map (22 sheets)

| Sheet | Fill when | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Overview | Always, first | Narrative, contacts, Design/Build approval blocks, Key Details (~30 fields: direction, source/target, file format, change detection, transmission/encryption/auth, retention 0-180d, trigger, frequency, dependencies, doc links). Flag "Contains PII" in Documentation & Related Links when applicable |
| Question | Always | Discovery Q&A (above) |
| Requirements | Always | Type (Assumption/Requirement/Enhancement/Constraint/Functional/Other), requirement, source, date, recorded-by, **Added to Test (Y/N/N-A)** - the traceability hook wd-testing uses |
| WD Solution - General / O4I / CC | Per type (macro) | Integration services, attributes, launch parameters, notifications (incl. standard `CF CT Integration Notification Message Content - Subject/Body` calc fields), security (ISSG/ISU/domains View-Modify-Get-Put), web services. O4I adds HTTP retries, XML namespaces, CSV format, error scenarios |
| Field Overrides - CC / Mappings - CC | Connector types | Field override services; map provider/name/default/exceptions |
| API | API/web-service payloads | 50 pre-numbered rows: element path, hardcoded/sample values, format, source, logic. Status per row: Researching -> Documented |
| File | Per file (duplicate the sheet for multiple files) | Format/delimiter/encoding header block + 50-row field grid (name, required, format, positions, Workday object/field, mapping, error handling) |
| Report | Per RaaS/custom report (duplicate per report) | Full report definition: data source + filters, columns, sort, filter logic, prompts |
| Calculated Fields | As needed | Top-level + supporting calc fields with the calc-field type-abbreviation dropdown (the 32-type list - wd-integration-dev `integration-naming.md` owns it); worked examples included - delete example rows before delivery |
| Custom Object | Per custom object | Object header + field grid (label, type, validations, web-service alias) |
| DIS | Per Data Initialization Service | DIS name (auto from Overview), output doc, population, schema, fields, maps |
| Mappings | Always if any value translation | Internal<->external value maps |
| Flow | Always | **Two diagrams, both required. (1) This Integration** - the integration process flow (source -> retrieve/trigger -> transform/validate -> deliver/write -> confirm/log, with the error/notification branch), the wd-design-visuals integration-flowchart variant. **(2) Broader Landscape** - REQUIRED when the integration is part of a package: show its relationship to the App/Vendor and the other associated integrations flowing into and out of Workday (e.g., an app + its 3 O4Is + the Workday modules/vendor each touches). A single integration with no siblings can mark the Broader Landscape "N/A - standalone integration." Embed both as images per SKILL.md (own clear block, no overlap) |
| Examples | Always | **Embed the real artifacts as OBJECT ATTACHMENTS in the sheet** (Insert -> Object -> Create from File, "Display as icon"): sample scripts (XSLT/Studio), vendor documents/specs, sample data files (**PII-scrubbed**), report definitions, SOAP request/response. Not just filenames or links - the reviewer should open them from the tab. If an artifact doesn't exist yet, yellow-flag a row naming what's expected and who owns it |
| Unit Testing | Always | COUNTIF status summary (target 95%), scenario grid, **12 pre-seeded standard scenarios** (connectivity, file-matches-spec, required fields, date/number formats, selection criteria, ISU security x3, value mapping, volume test) - keep them, add integration-specific ones (wd-testing derives) |
| Open Issues | Always | RAID items with links to the project RAID log (wd-pm / wd-smartsheet) |
| Knowledge | Always | KT rows: Cut Over Task / Maintenance Note / Troubleshooting / Run / Configuration Note - feeds wd-kt and wd-deployment cutover |

## Design-gate checklist (from the program checklist, generic items)

Before build starts: IDD named per naming standard (wd-integration-dev's integration-naming reference) and stored in the integration's folder with all technical artifacts (XSL/XSD, vendor docs, sample files, recordings); Question tab all Answered, highlights cleared; Overview contacts + approval blocks complete; About-the-Integration narrative covers the Workday future state; Requirements rows detailed (outbound population/filter criteria; inbound target objects) with sample rows removed; File tab field details complete; WD Solution tab names/ISU/ISSG/attributes/launch params entered; Flow diagram present; sample SOAP requests embedded; Unit Testing scenarios entered; Open Issues linked to the RAID log.

Plus the "IDD is a design doc" gate items above: READ ME present as CELLS (run `scripts/write_idd_readme.py` if missing; never a text box); yellow on every open/unanswered cell across all tabs; N/A (not blank) on reviewed-not-applicable cells; unused template rows + sample data cleaned (incl. the API Status column on empty rows); Flow tab has both the This-Integration flow and the Broader Landscape (or N/A-standalone); Examples holds embedded object attachments. **Sample data, field examples, and embedded/attached artifacts are synthetic or PII-scrubbed** - no real PHI/PII or secrets in a design doc that gets shared for review (owner rule: wd-extend-lifecycle `references/ai-data-governance.md` section 6).

**Mandatory pre-delivery gate - run the auditor.** Before ANY IDD version ships, run `python scripts/idd_audit.py <idd.xlsm>` and resolve every hit until it reports `[ok] no interior blanks` and `[ok] READ ME has cell content`. This is not optional and not an eyeball pass - a delivered IDD with a blank cell that isn't a value/N/A/yellow, or a missing READ ME, is a defect that costs the team's confidence in the deliverable.

**Mandatory pre-delivery gate #2 - FORMATTING (added 2026-08-06 after a client-facing miss).** `idd_audit.py` checks CONTENT completeness only; it says nothing about whether the page is readable. Also run:

```bash
python scripts/xlsx_format_audit.py <idd.xlsm>          # report
python scripts/xlsx_format_audit.py <idd.xlsm> --fix    # apply safe repairs
```

It flags five defects: **CLIPPED** (row too short for its wrapped text), **NOWRAP**, **VALIGN** (wrapped cells must be top-aligned so columns share a baseline), **IMG-OVERLAP** (checked in 2D - a row-only test false-positives on the header logo that legitimately sits beside the tab title), **CONTRAST** (text under 4.5:1 against its own fill, on every tab including READ ME and the macro-hidden tabs).

Then **VERIFY BY RENDER**: export a tab with `ws.ExportAsFixedFormat(0, path)` and rasterise with PyMuPDF, then LOOK at it. A property check is not evidence a page reads correctly - the worst defect found on the payroll IDD (a 767-char note in a 5-wide cell rendering as a giant band with one character per line) passed every property check.

Four traps this gate exists to catch:
- **Excel's AutoFit silently ignores merged cells.** A 2,236-char narrative in a merged block sat at 15pt and was cut off mid-sentence. Compute the needed height and set it explicitly; divide by the merge's row count when it spans rows.
- **Wrap thresholds must be relative to COLUMN WIDTH, not an absolute character count.** A 60-char rule missed a 36-char string in a narrow column, which rendered clipped.
- **Never grow a row to fit a long note in a narrow UNMERGED cell** - MERGE it across the table's column span instead. `xlsx_repair_wrap.py` reports this case rather than masking it.
- **Widen the column** when content genuinely needs width; don't force a tall row.

**(!) OLE object attachments are FRAGILE - verify them at the end of every session (2026-08-06).**
`OLEObjects.Add(Filename=...)` embedded nine files successfully, then began failing for **every
file and every path** later in the same session with `Add method of OLEObjects class failed`.
Ruled out: path length (a 64-char path fails too), Excel visibility, and a dead packager
(`ClassType="Package"` still succeeds, so the OLE server is alive - only the file-based embed path
breaks). Most likely COM/OLE state damage after repeated forced Excel terminations; it needs a
fresh session or a reboot to clear. Two consequences:

- **Never delete existing embeds before the replacements are proven.** Delete-then-Add loses the
  attachments outright if Add fails. Add first, verify the count, then remove the old ones.
- **Embeds are COPIES** - editing the source file afterwards does not update the workbook. Re-embed
  whenever a generated artifact changes, and re-verify the count before delivery.

Fallback when embedding will not cooperate: put a **clickable hyperlink** per artifact row
(`ws.Hyperlinks.Add(Anchor=cell, Address=<relative path>, TextToDisplay=<filename>)`). It keeps
file and description on the same row and one click opens the file, at the cost of the workbook
having to travel with its folder. State that tradeoff on the tab rather than leaving the reader to
discover a broken link, and log restoring the true attachments as an open item.

**Examples tab layout that reads well:** `# | Artifact | File | Status | What it is / why it
matters`, one artifact per row, the file link (or icon) in its own column so it sits beside its
description. The template's default - a prose note, a table, and all the attachment icons dumped
in a block underneath - gives the reader no way to tell which file is which. Also delete the
template's placeholder group shapes on that tab; they overlap whatever table you build.

**Branding (standing rule) - the neutral default; a client brand only when the engagement asks.** Style with `scripts/xlsx_brand_style.py` (`--brand-profile <client>` for a client look). When that client brand has a logo, place it on every sheet, hidden ones included, then re-anchor it:

```bash
python scripts/xlsx_place_wordmark.py <workbook> --brand-profile <client>
python scripts/xlsx_brand_style.py    <workbook> --brand-profile <client> --wordmark-only
```

The wordmark keeps the **locked aspect ratio** from the client's profile, so a naive swap cannot distort it. For wrap and row heights - including merged ranges, which Excel's AutoFit ignores - run `python scripts/xlsx_repair_wrap.py <workbook>`. Note the Extend `.xlsx` builder output contains no logo images at all, so only its fills/fonts are in scope there.

**COM reliability.** The full COM-vs-openpyxl rationale + the reliability gotchas (gen_py cache, late-bound Dispatch, retry-on-busy, iterate-by-index, orphaned-process/PID kill) live in one owner - [scripts.md](scripts.md) ("Why COM, not openpyxl"). Follow them for any COM edit to an IDD.

**(!) No working Excel COM? Convert EVERY formula to a static value after an openpyxl edit (2026-09-09).** On locked-down machines Excel COM automation is BLOCKED (`Workbooks.Open` fails even on a local copy) and there's no LibreOffice, so an IDD must be edited with **openpyxl** - and **openpyxl re-saving a formula makes Excel throw "Removed Records: Formula from /xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml" recovery on open** (the scary "found a problem" dialog), even when nothing else is wrong. The firm template's Unit Testing `COUNTIF` dashboard triggered it; client-specific IDD templates may add `=_xlfn.CONCAT(...)` ISU/ISSG auto-names + a COUNTIF/SUM/% dashboard + a DIS-name CONCAT. **Fix:** before delivery, scan for formula cells (`isinstance(c.value,str) and c.value.startswith("=")`) and replace each with its **static value** (COUNTIF->the count, CONCAT->the literal "ISU/ISSG INTxxxx Name", %/SUM->the computed number), then **reload the workbook and assert formulas==0**. Trade-off: the live dashboard + auto-naming stop updating - acceptable for a delivered vXX, note it. Editing an `.xlsm` this way: `load_workbook(p, keep_vba=True)` preserves the macros; write through a **merge-aware** helper that skips `MergedCell` objects (their `.value` is read-only - only the top-left anchor is writable). And **format-audit VALIGN(center) + IMG-OVERLAP flags on a client template are usually its OWN styling** (center-aligned cells + per-tab header logos), NOT defects - preserve them; only fix real CLIPPED (set row heights + enable wrap on the cells YOU populated).

Formatting, yellow-highlight, versioning, and change control follow this skill's standard conventions (SKILL.md / change-control.md).
